content: 1. Both levofloxacin and paliperidone can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored in patients receiving these medications concurrently. 2. Levofloxacin and panobinostat both significantly increase the QTc interval. Panobinostat is known to have a high risk of QT prolongation, and its prescribing information advises against co-administration with other QT-prolonging drugs. Alternative therapies should be considered. 3. Levofloxacin may reduce the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 4. Co-administration of levofloxacin and paroxetine can increase the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and patients should be closely monitored. 5. Levofloxacin and pasireotide both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 6. Levofloxacin and pazopanib may have a minor interaction that increases the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain. 7. Levofloxacin and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 8. Levofloxacin and perphenazine both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 9. Levofloxacin may decrease the effects of phenytoin through an unknown mechanism. There are also case reports of quinolones increasing phenytoin levels. Caution is advised, and monitoring is necessary. 10. Levofloxacin and pimozide both prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided, and alternative therapies should be considered. 11. Levofloxacin may enhance the effects of pioglitazone through pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution is advised, and patients should be monitored for potential adverse effects, including dysglycemia. 12. Administration of quinolone antibiotics, including levofloxacin, may result in hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. Gatifloxacin is most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is least likely. 13. Levofloxacin and ribociclib both prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided, and alternative therapies should be used. 14. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of levofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously with drugs that increase the risk of Torsades de Pointes. 15. Levofloxacin and risperidone both increase the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and patients should be monitored closely. 16. Levofloxacin and romidepsin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 17. Rose hips may decrease the levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative therapies should be considered. 18. Levofloxacin may enhance the effects of rosiglitazone through pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution is advised, and patients should be monitored for potential adverse effects, including dysglycemia. 19. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after levofloxacin to avoid chelation. 20. Sodium citrate/citric acid decreases the levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after levofloxacin. 21. Levofloxacin decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Additionally, these agents decrease levofloxacin levels through cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after levofloxacin to avoid magnesium chelation. 22. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride decreases the levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 23. Sorafenib and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and patients should be monitored closely. 24. Levofloxacin and sotalol both significantly increase the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided, and alternative therapies should be used. 25. Strontium ranelate decreases the levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Strontium ranelate should be suspended during antibiotic therapy.
